title: An American /r/
goal: Practise /r/ and use it in a short, understandable exchange.
cue: Keep your tongue from touching the ridge behind your upper teeth. Different comfortable tongue shapes can work. Slightly round the lips; avoid adding a tap or an extra vowel.
spelling: American English usually keeps r in car. Other English accents may use a different pattern.

articulation.label: rip
articulation.alt: rip: /r/ → /ɪ/ → /p/. Tongue, lips, contact and airflow positions.
notes: /r/: Bunch the tongue; leave space at the ridge.
/ɪ/: Front tongue, a little lower and relaxed.
/p/: Close the lips, then release the air.
articulation.note: Join the sounds smoothly after practising each position.
